pages.title: Cái này bao nhiêu?
pages.summary: Save this for markets, seafood trays, taxis, and any cash moment where the price needs to be visible before you commit.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Cái này bao nhiêu? is the pointing phrase for one visible thing: a mango, shirt, coffee, seafood tray, menu photo, or ride add-on. The phrase is small, but it protects the moment before money gets awkward.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Point first, say Cái này bao nhiêu?, then wait for the number to be spoken, typed, or shown on a calculator. Keep the item visible until the price is clear.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Listen to each piece, then the whole phrase, so the rhythm feels connected instead of memorized word by word.

sections.title: Natural variations
sections.body: Use these when the price question needs a softer tone, a total, or a clearer object. The pointing still does most of the work.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: The useful part is timing. Ask before the bag is packed, the plate is weighed, or the ride has started, then repeat or show the number back so both sides see the same price.

sections.title: Traveler insight
sections.body: The answer may be spoken fast, typed into a phone, shown on a calculator, or answered with a gesture. If the number matters, ask them to type it.

phrases.english: Can you lower it a little?

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Markets, snack stalls, small shops, beach seafood, laundry counters, and informal rides are where this earns its place. For several items, move to a total-price phrase before paying.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: If the answer comes too fast, hand over your phone calculator or point to theirs. Numbers are easier to trust when both people can see them.

pages.title: Quận Ba Đình

cityMetadata.rationale: Ba Dinh matters because it shows how Hanoi shifts from national symbols to ordinary blocks within a short ride or walk.

sections.title: Read The Facade

sections.title: A Central Short Detour

sections.title: Apartment Facade Is The Clue
sections.body: Cafes and boutiques change over time. The reliable clue is the old apartment facade on Nguyen Hue, with balconies stacked over the walking street.

sections.title: Same Building, Two Names
sections.body: You may see it called 42 Nguyen Hue or the Cafe Apartment. The address helps with maps; Cafe Apartment helps you picture the floor-by-floor browse.
